issues.description: Method mismatch: Lecture.addGuestStudents. The problem statement / UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int and a reason String). The template's TODO refers to adding addGuestStudents as specified in the UML but does not provide a signature. The solution implementation defines addGuestStudents(int) with a single int parameter. This inconsistency means students following the problem statement will implement a two-parameter method while the provided solution (and any tests derived from it) use a single-parameter method — causing compilation failures or test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Preferred option: change the solution's method signature to match the problem statement: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and implement handling of the reason (e.g., log it or store it in a field). If the educational intent was to accept only an int, update the problem statement and UML to require addGuestStudents(int) and update tests. Ensure template TODO (or starter file) documents the exact signature students must implement to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method named addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a reason String). The solution's Lecture class implements addGuestStudents(int) (only one int parameter). The template file contains a TODO for adding the addGuestStudents method but does not provide the signature. This mismatch between the required signature (int, String) in the problem/UML and the implemented signature (int) in the solution will confuse students about which method to implement and may cause compilation or test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make all artifacts agree on the method signature. Either (A) update the solution method to match the exercise and UML by changing the signature to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and handle or document the reason parameter (e.g., log it or store it), or (B) if the reason parameter was intentionally omitted, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) so the specification, template, and solution are consistent.
